newsitem.title: KENYA: Meeting of U.N. environment body ends in disarray.
newsitem.headline: Meeting of U.N. environment body ends in disarray.

text.p: A row over the reform of the U.N. environment agency boiled over on Friday night with the suspension of a key meeting and the United States, Britain and Spain threatening to withhold their 1997 budget contributions.
"This is a very sad night for diplomacy," Elizabeth Dowdeswell, executive director of the U.N. Environment Programme (UNEP), told Reuters.
Confounding expectations of compromise, the governing council of UNEP broke up in disarray on its last day after angry exchanges.
The divisive issue was a U.S.-backed proposal for the creation of a high-level committee to oversee UNEP, diminishing the role of permanent representatives of the agency's 185 member states.

"Until there is some satisfactory action, a number of governments including the United States, the United Kingdom and Spain will temporarily withhold their contributions to UNEP for 1997," said the head of the U.S. delegation, assistant secretary of state Eileen B. Claussen.
"In the end it was a dispute over who is in charge of UNEP," she told Reuters.

The three-day meeting of environment ministers at UNEP's headquarters in Nairobi was an acrimonious and inconclusive start to the campaign for a wholesale reform of the U.N. system pledged by new secretary-general Kofi Annan.
Dowdeswell, a Canadian heading the only global U.N. agency based in the Third World, said she would consult governments next week about when and where to reconvene the meeting.
She said the row had brought controversial issues on to the table after years of "papering over the cracks" at UNEP.
"So while tonight has been very sad in the long term it may be beneficial," Dowdeswell said.
Ironically, the governing body had agreed before the breakdown to strengthen UNEP's role and restore its status as the world's dominant environmental forum.
The past days saw dire warnings that UNEP was headed towards extinction unless it "reinvented" itself with a clearer mandate, a bigger budget and better management.
Before the meeting's suspension, the governing council approved a total budget for 1998/99 of $107.5 million, arresting a steady erosion of UNEP's funding during the 1990s.
Delegates including Claussen said the chaotic finale should not detract from progress achieved on subes such as control of dangerous chemicals.
The bone of contention was the plan to create a ministerial-level sub-committee, meeting regularly to supervise UNEP.
This drew the ire of some of the Nairobi-based diplomats in UNEP's Committee of Permanent Representatives (CPR) who saw their role reduced to that of "postmen", delegates said.
Instead of prolonging the talks to resolve the issue, the meeting's chairman, Arnaldo Gabaldon, suddenly suspended it and delegates rushed to the airport to catch their scheduled flights.
